params.body:
## What

Standard 0.9.0 (proposed): a Source gets a lifecycle, and the criteria that move it live in `rules/source.json` as data, like every other threshold in the standard.

- **States** (`ontology/states.json`): proposed, trial, admitted, muted, retired, rejected. Only admitted sources feed the record. A source on trial is collected and classified, but its signals are not promoted, do not count towards a pattern and cannot be cited.
- **A person admits, never a rule.** The machine's new `byPerson` list holds trial > admitted, unmute, retire and re-propose. `check.mjs` refuses a standard in which trial > admitted is not a person's move.
- **Criteria** (`rules/source.json`, executed by `tools/rules.mjs`):
  - entry: non-commercial or forbidden terms and duplicates are refused; unknown terms may still run a trial;
  - trial: 14 days, at least 10 signals, at most 25% failed runs, a kept share at least half the record's over the same window, and at least 20% of kept signals adding a concept the record lacks; a quiet source gets one extension;
  - admission: the trial says ready, and the terms are read and allow a paid product;
  - starting trust from editorial quality (high 1.2, standard 1.0, low 0.8; a report keeps 1.5);
  - mute after 25 failed runs in a row;
  - review: silent for 30 days, or kept below a quarter of the record's share over 90 days, puts the source in front of a person.
- **Verdicts carry reasons.** `sourceTrial` answers ready, needs-terms, not-yet or refuse, and every answer other than ready says why, so the approval screen can show the measurement instead of a model's opinion.
- **Source properties:** `access`, `terms`, `editorialQuality` and `audienceProximity` (two separate axes), `languages`, `proposedBy`, `admittedBy`, `admittedAt`, `stateReason`.

## Why

Today a source is proposed by a model-scored scout (score of 70 or more) and approved by switching `active` on. Nothing runs as a trial, nothing records who approved it, there is no field for terms of use (the ESS licence question lives in a design note), and a rejected proposal is deleted. Trust is a single number that many adapters hard-code.

Pipeline numbers for the 30 days to 9 October 2026, from the Observatory's Mix:
- 79,350 signals came in and 29% were kept;
- 254 sources delivered, and 86 of them delivered a signal that anything cites;
- six Chinese hot-rank lists account for 645 of the 877 cited signals;
- Google Trends delivered 16,034 signals, kept 11% and has 1 cited; Wikipedia spikes delivered 5,905, kept 6% and has none cited.

Under these rules, Google Trends would not pass a trial today and Wikipedia spikes would be flagged for review. The bars are relative to the record, so they move with the corpus.

## Compatibility

Added only. `tools/compat.mjs` reads every release from v0.1.0 to v0.8.0. A source written before 0.9.0 has no state: active reads as admitted and inactive as muted. `trust` and `tier` are unchanged.

## Open before a tag

- The numbers are first values. Two of them are editorial calls and belong to Trendwolves editorial: the scale of `editorialQuality` and the minimum share of new concepts (`minDistinctShare`).
- The pipeline does not read any of this yet. Its side is a separate change in gentells-pipeline: a `status` column with a backfill from `active`, measuring the trial, the approval screen on the Sources page, and keeping rejected rows instead of deleting them.

## Tests

`npm test`: 71 pass, 0 fail. This includes 20 new conformance cases (entry, trial, trust, mute, review) and three refusal tests.
params.title: 0.9.0 (proposed): source lifecycle and admission criteria as data
